text: Start with the inclusive integer range [3, 25]. First, discard every number that is not prime. Then, replace each remaining number with its remainder modulo 5, taken in the range 0 to 4. Finally, compute the mean of the remaining values, rounded to the nearest integer (round half to even).
Consider the integers from 2 to 32, inclusive. First, discard every number that is 16 or greater. Of these numbers, report the result of combining all remaining numbers with bitwise XOR.

Start with the inclusive integer range [34, 189]. First, keep only the numbers whose digits sum to 4. Then, replace each remaining number x with x * x. Finally, compute the product of all remaining values modulo 37 (the non-negative remainder).
Take all integers between 7 and 17, including both endpoints. First, discard every even number, keeping the odd ones. Finally, report the minimum of the remaining values.

Consider the integers from 4 to 184, inclusive. First, keep only the perfect squares. Then, reverse the decimal digits of each remaining number (reverse the digits of its absolute value, keep the original sign, and drop any leading zeros). Of these numbers, report how many numbers are left.

Consider the integers from 72 to 197, inclusive. First, keep only the numbers that contain the digit 3. Next, keep only the numbers that are strictly greater than 164. Then, replace every remaining value x with x squared. Then, replace every remaining value x with the digits of |x| written in reverse order, with the original sign restored and leading zeros dropped. Of these numbers, compute the bitwise XOR of all remaining values.

Take all integers between 11 and 48, including both endpoints. First, retain only the values whose decimal representation includes the digit 6. Then, replace each remaining number by reversing the digits of its absolute value, keeping the original sign and dropping any leading zeros. Then, replace each remaining number with the sum of its decimal digits (ignoring any minus sign). Finally, report how many remaining numbers equal 0.

Take all integers between 20 and 47, including both endpoints. First, keep only the numbers that are strictly less than 38. Next, replace each remaining number x with x mod 7, where the result lies in 0 to 6. Next, replace each remaining number x with 3 * x. Then, replace every remaining value x with the digits of |x| written in reverse order, with the original sign restored and leading zeros dropped. Of these numbers, report the number of unique values among the remaining numbers.
